newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal collapses, key technical reversal.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal collapses, key technical reversal.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures crumbled on Monday and chartists noted a bearish key technical reversal after USDA surprised the market by leaving ending soybean stocks unchanged at 125 million bushels, traders said.
"The market wanted to find new excitement in this report and they didn't find it, so (the longs) are all out the door," said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter.
Soyoil futures also ended lower, struggling with USDA's increase in projected soybean crush figures.
USDA increased its estimate for the U.S. crush this year by five million bushels to 1.425 million.
But soybean imports were also raised by five million bushels to 10 million, leaving ending stocks unchanged.
That scenario weighed more heavily on soyoil than soymeal because oil demand has been lagging meal usage, traders said.

Locals started the selling frenzy in soybeans which spilled over into soymeal. Chartists noted the May contract set a fresh contract high earlier in the session but closed sharply lower, suggesting a key technical reversal.
Soymeal ended $8.50 to $1.00 per ton lower with July off $8.50 at $285.80. Soyoil ended 0.44 to 0.25 cent per lb lower with July down 0.43 at 24.27.
"There was a huge technical reversal in meal," a pit source said. "We set a contract high but took out the (session) low. All the discussion this afternoon has been focused on that."

Contract highs were notched in the May, July, August and September soymeal in morning trade after USDA said weekly soybean export inspections totaled 12.536 million bushels, above expectations for six million to 10 million bushels.
The new high for the May is $308.50, topping the previous high of $305.40 set on Friday and the highest for a nearby contract since 1988.
Forecasts for a cool week in the U.S. Midwest lent support to new crop on the belief that seedings would be slowed.
On the day, Continental Grain sold 500 lots July soymeal, LIT sold 300 December and 100 July, and Smith Barney and Rosenthal Collins each sold 200 July.
In soyoil, E.D. and F. Man International sold 500 July, Cargill Inc sold 300 July and bought 400 July and Rosenthal Collins sold 250 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 31,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 27,804 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 16,000 lots, against Friday's 12,004.
